title: Error by AI scribe during medical appointment leaves patient devastated

reports.title: Error by AI scribe during medical appointment leaves patient devastated

summary:
Rebecca Green agreed to have an artificial intelligence tool transcribe her first urologist appointment, but it invented a claim that she micro-dosed psychedelic mushrooms. She discovered the false statement after kidney stone surgery in March, when a post-operative letter to her GP said mushroom use might explain earlier kidney bleeding. Ms Green, who was receiving workers' compensation, feared the error could harm her case. Her urologist later apologised, corrected the record, and said she would review how AI was used in her practice.

A report by Digital Rights Watch found AI medical scribes are often unregulated and can make serious mistakes, such as recording the wrong breast in a cancer diagnosis or inventing epilepsy. The Royal Australian College of GPs estimates 40 per cent of GPs regularly use these tools, a figure considered conservative. Australia's Therapeutic Goods Administration has been reviewing AI scribes and will release findings in coming weeks, with breaches to be acted upon. Digital Rights Watch wants the AI Safety Institute to test and approve tools.
